voice_design: Plain, warm, ordinary. He asks direct questions that expose family phrases without turning into a therapist. He uses contemporary town talk, music, school, and practical care.
default_address: Mara by name; light teasing only after reciprocity; no pet name used as ownership.
trust_language: Honesty in small pieces, keeping promises, accepting ordinary help.
pressure_language: Frustration with ambiguity; “Who is this we?”; rescuer logic when patience runs out.
small_talk_triggers: Bands, choir, movies, seatbelts, burgers, the town radio, fixing a Jeep.
transformed_example: “You keep saying ‘we.’ I’m asking what you want tonight.”
state_rule: He can remain kind while setting distance. Romance is optional and never the reward for disclosure.
guardrail: Avoid making him the enlightened savior. His ordinary assumptions can also misread Mara.

source_voice: Dr. Kerry, Professor Steinberg, David Runciman and other mentors
voice_design: Precise, spare, intellectually demanding. She asks one question at a time, names assumptions, and distinguishes evidence from interpretation.
default_address: Ms. Vale at first; Mara only after invitation; colleagues by surname/title.
trust_language: Preparation, intellectual risk, admitting what is not known, revising a claim.
pressure_language: Can move too quickly, assume access to resources, or turn pain into an interesting problem.
small_talk_triggers: A note in the margin, an odd source, a building’s history, a student’s practical analogy.
transformed_example: “Your account is not weaker because it changed. Show me what changed it.”
state_rule: Her praise is specific and rare; access expands through work rather than flattery.
guardrail: Mentorship must not erase Mara’s authorship or become magical rescue.

voice_design: Quiet moral language, deliberate pauses, practical offers. He can quote scripture without using it to close questions. He knows community gossip but resists feeding it.
default_address: Sister Vale in public; Mara in private after trust; Brother/Sister for congregants.
trust_language: Service, confidentiality, sincerity, willingness to protect someone publicly.
pressure_language: Overvaluing reconciliation, delaying action, protecting institutional calm.
small_talk_triggers: Choir practice, casseroles, shelter supplies, whose porch needs repair, a hymn’s history.
transformed_example: “A belief should make care more exact
guardrail: His credibility grows only when private listening becomes public responsibility.
source_locator: Religion must not collapse into Abel’s version; include beauty, ritual, service, hesitation, and disagreement.

source_voice: Police, clerks, doctors, county and public systems
voice_design: Calm, short procedural questions; separates immediate safety, witness accounts, and legal proof. Uses names and timestamps.
default_address: Ms. Vale/Mara; sir/ma’am under stress; no folksy pet names.
trust_language: Specific facts, preserved evidence, admitting uncertainty, following through.
pressure_language: Cold forms, repeated questions, institution-first assumptions.
small_talk_triggers: Road closures, weather, vehicle registration, county records, who called dispatch.
transformed_example: “Tell me what you saw before anyone explained it to you.”
state_rule: Institutional trust grows through useful action and honest limits, not automatic virtue.
guardrail: Show bureaucracy’s friction as well as its protective value.

source_voice: Town peers, performers and work competitors
voice_design: Quick banter, confident slang, public energy, competitive framing. She notices presentation and performance before hidden motives.
default_address: Mara by shortened name; playful titles earned through actions.
trust_language: Showing up, taking a fair risk, warning a rival, sharing the stage.
pressure_language: Public teasing, dares, treating hesitation as weakness.
small_talk_triggers: Auditions, costumes, race times, salvaged parts, who is leaving town first.
transformed_example: “You can take the safe route. Just don’t call it the fast one when I beat you there.”
state_rule: Teasing must stop when a boundary is stated if the relationship is healthy.
guardrail: Do not blur healthy rivalry with Silas’s coercive pattern.

voice_design: Polished, reassuring, metric-driven; turns risk into schedule language and workers into capacity. Rarely raises his voice.
default_address: First names to simulate equality; titles when leveraging officials.
trust_language: Speed, deliverables, plausible deniability, private favors.
pressure_language: “Temporary measure,” “acceptable loss,” “everyone signed off,” scarcity deadlines.
small_talk_triggers: Contracts, fuel prices, inspection dates, equipment financing, county politics.
transformed_example: “I’m not asking you to skip safety. I’m asking whether the job survives a six-hour delay.”
state_rule: His friendliness persists even as consequences accumulate; evidence changes leverage, not his conscience overnight.
guardrail: Keep him systemic. He does not explain away family control or become a boss-fight villain.
source_locator: Inspired by recurring labor/economic pressures across Chs. 6, 14–16, 19–20.
